title: Random survival forest with inflammation index stratifies oropharyngeal cancer survival
summary: A random survival forest was developed on 568 Roswell Park oropharyngeal cancer patients treated with radiation and validated on 421 patients from Ohio State. C-indices were 0.758 (full RSF), 0.725 (reduced) and 0.702 (decision tree); a model using SIRI, performance status and smoking history defined three risk groups that stratified overall and progression-free survival in the external cohort. The study is retrospective with modest discrimination.
ai_technology: Random survival forest and decision tree models using the systemic inflammation response index

evidence.tested: External validation in an independent cohort of 421 patients.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance is not reported; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Modeled survival and defined risk groups from pre-treatment bloodwork and clinical variables.
